name: Acute Compartment Syndrome
definition: Pathologic rise in pressure within a closed muscle compartment causing impaired tissue perfusion and risk of irreversible muscle/nerve damage.

redFlags.item: Any suspected acute compartment syndrome is a surgical emergency

core: Pulses do not rule out the diagnosis

investigations.principle: Diagnosis is clinical, supported by pressure measurement when uncertainty exists.
investigations.MRI: MRI is not appropriate when emergency ACS is suspected.
investigations.radiographs: Radiographs identify associated fracture but do not diagnose ACS.

amber: Do not delay decompression for imaging, analgesic trials or Ayurvedic treatment.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Any Shotha/Vedana description is secondary; emergency fasciotomy pathway takes priority.

patientEducation.summary: Pathologic rise in pressure within a closed muscle compartment causing impaired tissue perfusion and risk of irreversible muscle/nerve damage.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise, rapidly escalating pain or other listed red flags.
